title: Double particles: には, にも, とは and の + particle
summary: There is no such thing as a combined particle. Logical and non-logical particles can sit together; two logical particles cannot.

blocks.text: Lists of "particle combinations" make you memorize which can pair with which. You do not need them. Every particle just does its own job. Two facts explain all the pairings.

The five main **logical** particles are **が, を, に, で, へ**. They say what role each noun plays in the sentence: who does it, what it is done to, where, to what. A noun has one role, so **two logical particles cannot stand together**. The **non-logical** particles **は** and **も** do not give a role; they only make a topic or sub-topic. They fit beside a logical particle with no clash.

**が** (main carriage) and **を** (direct object) are so basic that nothing can be put next to them. To make such a noun a topic, **drop** the particle and put は or も alone. さくらをなぐった becomes さくらはなぐった, and the missing を is understood. You never see をは or がは.

rows: 冬には雪が降る (in winter, at least)
春にも雪が降る (in spring too)
topic and contrast at a place

blocks.text: In 明日学校に行く, に is needed to show the destination. 明日学校には行く says "as for school, I will go (but maybe not somewhere else)". 明日学校にも行く says "I will go to school too". The logical particle gives the role, and は or も adds a feeling.
The **nominalizing の** turns whatever comes before it into a noun, and a noun can take any logical particle: 泳ぐのが好きだ, 泳ぐのを見た, 泳ぐのに疲れた.

blocks.jp: この町にも図書館がある。
blocks.en: This town has a library as well.

blocks.jp: 友達と一緒に走るのが楽しい。
blocks.en: Running together with a friend is fun.

items: Logical: **が を に で へ**. Non-logical: **は も**.
Two logical particles never combine; a logical plus は or も does.
**が** and **を** drop away when は or も takes over.
**の** (the noun box) can be followed by any logical particle.

questions.instruction: Which pair is made up of logical particles only?
questions.note: が, を, に, で, へ are logical; は and も are not.
も only sets a topic.

questions.instruction: Why can you not say さくらをはなぐった?
options: を cannot be combined; use は alone
questions.note: The direct particles drop away when は takes over.

questions.instruction: Why can の take any logical particle?
options: It turns the clause into a noun
questions.note: A noun can take any role marker.

questions.en: In summer, (I) go to the sea.
questions.note: に gives the time, and は sits beside it as the topic.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap: "at that shop, too"
questions.prompt: あの店＿＿野菜を売っている。
questions.en: They sell vegetables at that shop, too.
questions.note: Selling happens at a place, so で; も adds "too".
と is logical and は sits beside it; the others stack logical particles.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that is a place plus a topic
questions.en: Please be quiet in the library.
questions.note: で marks the place and は makes it a topic.
で gives the place, も adds "too"; を stays with the object.

questions.instruction: True or false? After the nominalizing の you can attach が, を or に.
questions.note: の makes a noun, and a noun can take any logical particle.
The boxed clause is the carriage of 楽しい, so が.
What you saw is the object, so を follows の.

options: (I) will go only to his room
(I) will go to my brother's room, too
questions.en: (I) will go to my brother's room, too.
questions.note: に shows the destination and も adds "also".

options: By train, at least, I won't go (maybe by other means)
I will go by train, too
questions.en: (I) won't go by train (but maybe some other way).
questions.note: で marks the means; は adds contrast.
が and を are both logical, so they cannot stand together.

questions.prompt: On Sunday, at least, (I) will go to the park.
questions.en: On Sunday, at least, (I) will go to the park.
questions.note: に gives the time and は adds contrast; に marks the destination.

questions.instruction: 魚 is what in this sentence, and what happened to its particle?
options: The carriage; が was replaced by は
The object; を was replaced by は
A place; で was replaced by は
A goal; に was replaced by は
questions.en: (As for fish, I don't eat it.)
questions.note: The fish is eaten, so it is the object; を drops away when は takes over.

questions.instruction: Tap the word with a place particle plus も
questions.en: There is a house on top of the mountain, too.
questions.note: に shows where it exists and も adds "too".

options: At home, (I) don't study, though maybe elsewhere
questions.en: At home, (I) don't study (but maybe elsewhere).
questions.note: で marks the place, and は contrasts it with other places.

questions.prompt: (I) like reading books in the library.
questions.en: (I) like reading books in the library.
questions.note: の boxes 本を読む, and が marks it as what is liked.

questions.instruction: Why is に kept in 公園にも行く?
options: に shows the destination; も only adds "also"
に is needed only in the past
questions.note: A logical particle gives the role; は and も sit beside it.
に gives the time, and は adds the topic.
と means "with"; は sits beside it as the topic.

questions.instruction: Tap the word where の makes a clause into a noun with a role particle
questions.note: 歌うの is a noun box, and が marks it.
